item.content:encoded:
News / GuruFocus / Intuit Stocks Fall 7.17% Two Days Before Earnings as AI Finance Tools Loom

Intuit Stocks Fall 7.17% Two Days Before Earnings as AI Finance Tools Loom Less than 1 min read

INTU Intuit INTU dropped 7.17% to $320.79 at the 4:00 p.m. ET close on November 17 as the software selloff collided with worries that AI assistants could take over personal finance tasks. Startup Fortune linked the pressure to Anthropic's Personal Finance in Claude beta, which lets users connect bank accounts and query two years of transactions. Intuit reports fiscal first-quarter results on November 19 after the close. Its own guidance calls for revenue of $4.294 billion to $4.313 billion, up 11%, and non-GAAP EPS of $2.44 to $2.48. For fiscal 2027, the company expects revenue growth of only 9% to 10% after 14% in fiscal 2026, alongside non-GAAP EPS of $22.88 to $23.12, with TurboTax revenue having grown just 7% last year.

The midpoint EPS guide puts the shares at about 13.9 times forward earnings, a multiple that already assumes slower growth. GuruFocus gives Intuit a GF Score of 81/100, combining elite profitability with badly broken momentum. Its GF Value of $840.52 puts the close about 62% below the model, a significantly undervalued reading that likely reflects years of premium multiples the market no longer grants. Thursday's report is the immediate test: a beat with steady fiscal 2027 guidance could ease disruption fears, while any cut would validate them.

item.content:encoded:
News / GuruFocus / Sandisk Leads Tech Stocks in Earnings Surprises Ahead of 8-for-1 Split

Sandisk Leads Tech Stocks in Earnings Surprises Ahead of 8-for-1 Split Less than 1 min read

SNDK Sandisk (SNDK, Financials) recorded the largest earnings-per-share surprise among technology companies in a Seeking Alpha quantitative screen as the third-quarter earnings season approached its conclusion. The memory and storage giant topped analysts' consensus earnings projection by $3.10 a share, putting it ahead of other technology companies benefitting from sustained investment in computer infrastructure. Salesforce came in second with a $2.63 EPS surprise and American Bitcoin was third with a $2.34 surprise. Dell Technologies was fourth with a $2.12 surprise and Micron Technology rounded out the top five with $1.60. Other businesses beating estimates were Arrow Electronics at $1.26, InterDigital at $1.24 and Sanmina at $1.16. Ubiquiti and SharonAI Holdings completed the top 10 with shocks of $1.07 and $1.03, respectively. The list includes memory, corporate software and computer hardware and digital infrastructure, a reflection of better-than-expected profitability in a host of technological sectors. Investment in artificial intelligence continues to be a major industrial driver. Gartner's August projection projects global semiconductor sales to reach over $1.56 trillion in 2026, increasing 92% from 2025. An EPS surprise is the difference between reported profits per share and the average forecast of analysts. Investors will be eyeing next earnings projections and AI infrastructure expenditure patterns to assess if these profit beats are a sign of continued growth.

WSDT introduces prop trading for crypto and tokenized US stocks 2 min read

One-step challenges start at $19, with a free demo and weekly competitions available in the same trading terminal DUBAI, UAE, November 18, 2026 – WSDT is introducing its prop trading platform for cryptocurrency perpetual futures, gold and tokenized US stocks. Traders can access these markets through a single simulated account, with one-step evaluations starting at a one-time fee of $19 for a $1,500 account. The platform combines crypto perpetual futures, including Bitcoin and Ethereum, with xStocks instruments tracking companies such as Apple, NVIDIA and Tesla, alongside stock-index ETFs. Perpetual futures are contracts without an expiry date; xStocks track the prices of underlying shares or ETFs. On WSDT, these instruments are traded in a simulated environment, without ownership of the underlying shares or tokens. Positions across the markets share the same account balance and count toward the same evaluation. Traders can work across crypto and equity-linked instruments in one terminal while managing a single set of account limits. One evaluation, published trading rules A WSDT challenge tests trading performance against a 10% profit target, a 4% daily loss limit and a 6% maximum drawdown fixed against the starting account size. Traders must trade on at least four separate days, with no deadline to complete the evaluation. Account sizes range from $1,500 to $200,000, with fees varying by size. Traders who pass move to a funded-stage account, which is also simulated and retains the loss limits. They receive 80% of eligible profits under WSDT’s Provider Service Agreement. The evaluation fee pays for access to the challenge; it is not a trading deposit. Free ways to try the platform Registered users can open a free 14-day demo with a $100,000 simulated balance, without providing a payment card or making a deposit. The demo uses the same terminal as challenges, allowing traders to practice before entering an evaluation. Demo results do not qualify for payouts. WSDT also runs an ongoing weekly competition with free entry. Every participant starts with a $240,000 simulated balance, and the top three finishers receive challenge accounts. A new round opens each Monday at noon New York time. Winners must pass their awarded challenge before progressing to the funded stage. Registration, account options and full challenge rules are available on the WSDT website. About WSDT WSDT provides trader evaluation and educational services across crypto, gold and tokenized equity instruments. Built by TEFS, a prop trading firm established in 2017, it is operated by TEFS Marketing Management L.L.C. in Dubai, UAE. All WSDT trading accounts are simulated. Contact WSDT support@wsdt.com

AngloGold Ashanti, Coeur Mining, DRDGOLD, Gold Fields, and Hecla Mining Company shares are falling, what you need to know 1 min read

XAUUSD SI1!

What happened? A number of stocks fell in the morning session after precious metals tumbled as expectations of Federal Reserve interest rate hikes drew investors away from non-interest-bearing assets. CNBC reported that gold fell to its lowest level in more than a year, with gold futures falling 2.34% to $3,761.84 and spot gold down 2.38% at $3,758. The report also showed that silver fell to a 52-week low, as silver futures declined 3.5% to $45.72 and spot silver shed 3.6% to $45.67. Separately, CNBC reported that October 2026 U.S. retail sales excluding gas and autos rose 0.6%, exceeding expectations of 0.4%, while traders priced in a 95% chance of a quarter-percentage-point Federal Reserve interest rate hike, according to the CME Group’s FedWatch tool. The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks. Among others, the following stocks were impacted: Precious metals mining company AngloGold Ashanti fell 7.3%. Precious metals mining company Coeur Mining fell 5.3%. Precious metals mining company DRDGOLD fell 6.4%. Precious metals mining company Gold Fields fell 7.4%. Precious metals mining company Hecla Mining Company fell 4.9%.
